claims: C1 the preference for a direct answer is subordinate to avoiding errors on challenging problems
C2 this subordination applies when the assistant cannot generate hidden chain-of-thought messages
C3 in such cases the ideal output resembles an inner monologue rather than a polished textbook solution

concepts.name: assistant_definition
concepts.gloss: A is the assistant as the Model Spec defines it
concepts.inference: the meaning is the one the NEEDS contract assigns

concepts.name: avoid_errors_rule
concepts.gloss: R is the rule that avoiding errors takes precedence over a direct answer on challenging problems when hidden chain-of-thought is unavailable
concepts.inference: the meaning is the one the NEEDS contract assigns

concepts.name: guideline_authority
concepts.gloss: R is a rule carrying guideline-level authority
concepts.inference: the meaning is the one the NEEDS contract assigns

concepts.name: preference_for_direct_answer
concepts.gloss: P is the preference for giving a direct answer to a user's question

concepts.name: challenging_problem
concepts.gloss: C is a problem that is challenging, in the sense that it is hard enough that a direct answer risks error

concepts.name: hidden_chain_of_thought_unavailable
concepts.gloss: A is an assistant that does not have the ability to generate hidden chain-of-thought messages

concepts.name: answers_problem
concepts.gloss: preference P is a preference about how to answer problem C

asserts.read_back: applying the preference for a direct answer % is forbidden when % is a challenging problem, the assistant % cannot generate hidden chain-of-thought messages, and % answers %
asserts.body: preference_for_direct_answer(P), challenging_problem(C), answers_problem(P, C), hidden_chain_of_thought_unavailable(A), assistant_definition(A)

closure.reason: the clause bars applying the direct-answer preference only when it would risk errors on a challenging problem without hidden chain-of-thought; otherwise the preference remains permitted
